note: Human review confirms ako 'falar/dizer' is extended intransitive: when the addressee/interlocutor (the person spoken to/with) is expressed, it is obligatorily selected with the postposition ji. Development examples include FWFFG-031 (aire) and criacao_13 (ei, lemma ji). Clausal reported-speech complements are compatible with this lexical frame. Grammar-v2 must encode selected_oblique=ji for the addressee.
Development evidence includes overt ji-marked oblique in FWFFG-010; retain reviewed v1 frame.
Development shows indexed predicate without core object; locative material is oblique; retain reviewed v1 frame.

Human review confirms tu means 'ir' and is intransitive/monovalent. The moving participant is S; destination/location expressions are oblique rather than core objects. Development examples include Itumode, uture, and tudure. Grammar-v2 licenses tu as a monovalent motion predicate.

Confirmed in review sequence 2026-09-24 as monovalent motion/arrival predicate with indexed S. Linguist correction: Fabrício akaregodumode = 'Fabrício chegará'; Akaregodumode = 'você chegará'. Conditional whole-sentence translations are not evidence for conditional semantics of the verb form.
Development examples support subject-indexed motion predicate; interrogative location is oblique.
FWFFG-0102 has theme object and ji-marked recipient; retain reviewed v1 divalent classification, with recipient separately oblique.

Human review corrects the development-only provisional analysis: ro is transitive/divalent. The absence of an overt object in clean examples such as Irore oino does not license a monovalent analysis; these are compatible with an unexpressed object. Grammar-v2 must encode an object slot for ro.

Human review confirms lexical verbal to is transitive/divalent. Crucially, Bororo also has a homophonous postposition to; these must be represented as distinct lexical entries/uses. For example, baru to can mean 'ao céu', with to as a postposition, and must not be treated as evidence for verbal to or as an object construction. Grammar-v2 licenses only VERB to as divalent and must keep ADP/postposition to separate.
Confirmed by linguist 2026-09-24: monovalent existential/locative predicate; S is indexed and locative constituent is oblique.

Confirmed by linguist 2026-09-24: aidu 'gostar, querer' is extended intransitive. CGPB-p19.3 shows ji-marked participant. Clausal-complement use in CGPB-p19.1 is constructional behavior compatible with the lexical classification; criacao_11 UD obj annotation does not override the reviewed frame.

Conflicting development annotations: FWFFG-008 has imedu as obj, while FWFFG-0104 has Fabrício ji as obl and FWFFG-0103 also associates ji with jorudu. No grammar-v2 license assigned pending linguistic adjudication.

Human review confirms that an overt heard participant/content may be selected with postposition ji. However, postpositional complement selection alone does not establish the Bororo extended-intransitive class, which is defined by a specific semantic participant-role configuration. The earlier automatic promotion to extended_intransitive is withdrawn. Frame classification remains pending semantic-role adjudication; selected_complement_postposition=ji is retained as an independent fact.

Development mixes noncausative 'learn' (FWFFG-004), a translated 'teach' use (FWFFG-003), and overt causative eruduwado (FWFFG-006). Frame cannot be safely collapsed into one lexical license without analysis of derivation/causativization; excluded from grammar-v2 for now.

Human review confirms divalent frame. The apparent lack of overt object indexing is expected because 3SG object is zero-marked; kaboba/ioguduba (0066a-b) and ki (0067i) are object participants. Do not interpret zero exponence as absence of object coding.

Human review confirms aiwo is intransitive. It may additionally take a complement marked by the postposition ji. This postpositional complementation must not be used to classify aiwo as an extended intransitive; that class depends on a specific semantic participant-role configuration. Grammar-v2 records intransitivity and optional/possible ji-marked complementation as separate properties.

Human review confirms base akedu is intransitive/monovalent. The causative akedudo (surface etagedudo in development) is transitivized/divalent and may take an overt object. Keep the lexical frame of akedu separate from the valency-changing causative derivation; the object annotation in 017.KJB does not override the reviewed base frame.

Human review confirms okwage 'comer' is intransitive/monovalent. The earlier proposal of extended-intransitive status based on nearby postpositional material is rejected. Development evidence must not be used to infer an additional core argument merely from co-occurring ji. Grammar-v2 licenses okwage as intransitive.

Development re-supports the reviewed v1 monovalent frame. meru occurs with indexed S and no core object: amerumode in a locative/interrogative hunting context and pamerumode 'we/you.PL will go home' in 086.EncIE. The du ji sequence in 0057e belongs to the embedding/complement construction and is not evidence for a lexical object of meru.

Human review confirms kado 'cortar/interromper' is transitive/divalent. The participant/event that is cut or interrupted occupies the object slot. Development examples with karo 'fish' as object support this classification; clausal/eventive uses do not require a separate monovalent frame.

Human review confirms base pega 'ser ruim/mau' is intransitive/monovalent. The derived causative pegado is transitive/divalent. Grammar-v2 must represent this as a valency-changing causative derivation and must not use objects of pegado to assign transitive valency to the base pega.

Human review confirms rema is the copula used for identificational predicates: the two nominal expressions have the same referent. Keep this construction distinct from lexical verbal valency and from existential/locative predication. Development examples FWFFG-019 and FWFFG-035 support same-referent identification; translations alone must not broaden rema into a general existential copula. ABE evidence remains sealed and unused.

Development independently re-supports the reviewed v1 divalent frame for towuje 'make/create'. criacao_06 has objects kare and boe; criacao_15 has Satanae and bope; sabia.001 has kiogorogu 'little bird' as object. The consistent pattern is creator/agent plus created theme. Retain the reviewed v1 license.

Human review confirms rakoje is an intransitive verb meaning 'estar em pé' ('be/stand upright'), not a postposition. It therefore has a monovalent lexical frame. Development examples with juko/joru as S are compatible with this analysis; locative/postpositional material is non-core. The earlier postposition correction is superseded by this human-reviewed decision.

Human review confirms base pemega 'ser bom' is intransitive/monovalent. The derived causative pemegado is transitive/divalent. Grammar-v2 must represent the causative as a valency-changing derivation and must not project the transitive frame of pemegado onto base pemega.

Human review on 2026-09-24 explicitly leaves the lexical frame unresolved ('não sei (ainda)'). Development evidence is insufficient to promote ciri to a grammar-v2 license. The previous monovalent proposal based on baru kuru ciri is withdrawn. Keep ciri excluded from the frozen operational grammar until independent linguistic analysis establishes its valency.

Human review confirms rutu = 'subida/subir' (ascent/go up) and an intransitive monovalent frame. The participant undergoing upward motion is S; goals/locations are expressed as oblique/postpositional phrases, not core objects.

Development re-supports reviewed v1 barigu 'throw'. CGPB-p50.1 has an implicit 3SG object ('Eu o joguei') plus goal moto kae; CGPB-p51.1 and 0086a.PessGr show reflexive/reciprocal realization of the theme. The absence of an overt object NP in p50.1 is compatible with zero realization of 3SG.O and must not be interpreted as monovalency. Singleton Crowell evidence is excluded.

Human review confirms reru 'dançar' is intransitive/monovalent. The dancer is S and no object slot is licensed. Development examples are compatible with this analysis, including ererure and embedded ereruidu.

Human review confirms kudu 'beber' is extended intransitive: when the drink/theme argument is overt, it is selected with the postposition ce. The development occurrence ikuduwo 'para eu beber' has no overt theme and is compatible with argument omission. Grammar-v2 must encode selected_oblique=ce for kudu rather than treating the theme as a direct object.

Human review corrects the provisional monovalent analysis: aimo 'banhar(-se)' is lexically reflexive in the relevant construction. It has an object slot, but that slot is obligatorily co-referential with the subject and is filled by the same person index. The correct form is Cere cedaimo. It shows ce- in the subject expression Cere and the corresponding ce- reflexive/object indexing in cedaimo; the corpus form cetaimo is therefore not used as the normative realization. Grammar-v2 must model this as a reflexive divalent frame with subject-object coindexation, not as ordinary monovalency.
